raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

GRPO / any v1 rollout with **DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen** models fails for every prompt with:

```
ValueError: Tokenizer does not define required token '<|im_end|>'
```

and validation then dies with the misleading `ValueError: Received an empty list as keys.`

Continuous Token builder selection is an exact lookup on the root `config.json` `model_type`, and `qwen2` maps to the Qwen ChatML builder. R1-Distill-Qwen reports `model_type: qwen2` but ships a DeepSeek tokenizer without the ChatML tokens.

This PR falls back to the default builder (with a warning) when the family was **auto-resolved** to a Qwen text family and the tokenizer does not define `<|im_end|>`. An explicit `model_family=qwen` still raises, so a real misconfiguration is not hidden.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+continuous+token , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+R1-Distill (no existing fix found; related builder work: #7630, #7628)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

**Unit tests (CPU, picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`):** `tests/utils/test_continuous_token_on_cpu.py`: 172 passed. New cases: auto-resolved fallback, explicit `model_family=qwen` still raises, unk-mapped id, unk id returned as a one-element list, the unk token itself is still accepted.

**Real tokenizer (CPU):** `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B` (`model_type: qwen2`, no `<|im_end|>` in vocab), `create_continuous_token_builder(tok, hf_model_type="qwen2")`:
- `main`: `ValueError: Tokenizer does not define required token '<|im_end|>'`
- this PR: warning `Auto-resolved Continuous Token family qwen requires '<|im_end|>' but the tokenizer does not define it; falling back to default.` → `ContinuousTokenBuilder`

**End-to-end (CUDA, A100 80GB; torch 2.13 + cu130, vllm 0.29, transformers 5.12.1).** DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (same tokenizer as the 7B), gsm8k, v1 trainer, GRPO:

| Run | This PR | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 GPU, 2 steps | exit 0; fallback warning logged, 0 × `required token` | every rollout: `Tokenizer does not define required token '<\|im_end\|>'` |
| 1 GPU, `val_before_train=True` | – | rollouts fail as above, then `ValueError: Received an empty list as keys.` |
| 2 GPUs, actor `fsdp2`, 2 steps | exit 0; fallback logged, no `required token` error | – |

To reproduce:

<details>
<summary>Shared setup and base command (used by the runs below)</summary>

```bash
python3 examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py --local_dir $HOME/data/gsm8k
hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --local-dir $HOME/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
hf download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B --local-dir $HOME/models/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B

NGPU=${NGPU:-1}
COMMON=(
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False
  "data.train_files=['$HOME/data/gsm8k/train.parquet']" "data.val_files=['$HOME/data/gsm8k/test.parquet']"
  data.train_batch_size=8 data.max_prompt_length=256 data.max_response_length=256
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True data.truncation=error
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=4
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=False actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=2
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.3 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=2
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=2 actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=2
  trainer.balance_batch=True 'trainer.logger=["console"]' trainer.project_name=repro
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPU trainer.nnodes=1 trainer.save_freq=-1 trainer.test_freq=-1
  trainer.val_before_train=False trainer.total_epochs=1 trainer.use_v1=True
)
```
</details>

```bash
MODEL=$HOME/models/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
GRPO=(algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo actor_rollout_ref.model.path=$MODEL +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_model_len=1024)

# training run (on main every rollout fails with the missing-token error)
python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo "${COMMON[@]}" "${GRPO[@]}" trainer.total_training_steps=2 2>&1 | tee grpo_r1.log
grep -c "Tokenizer does not define required token" grpo_r1.log   # this PR: 0
grep -c "falling back to default" grpo_r1.log                    # this PR: > 0

# validation path (on main: "Received an empty list as keys.")
python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo "${COMMON[@]}" "${GRPO[@]}" trainer.total_training_steps=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True data.val_max_samples=16

# tokenizer only, no GPU
python3 -c "
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from verl.utils.tokenizer.continuous_token_wiring import create_continuous_token_builder
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B')
print(type(create_continuous_token_builder(tok, hf_model_type='qwen2')).__name__)"

# 2 GPUs: set NGPU=2 before building COMMON and append actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy=fsdp2
```

Not evaluated: whether the default builder gives exactly the right token boundaries for R1-Distill multi-turn rollouts. This PR removes the hard failure; it does not add an R1-Distill-specific builder.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. `model_family="auto"` (the default) now degrades gracefully for Qwen-architecture models with a non-ChatML tokenizer; `model_family="qwen"` keeps the strict check.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/tokenizer/continuous_token_wiring.py`: when the family was auto-resolved to a Qwen text family and `_tokenizer_defines_token(tokenizer, "<|im_end|>")` is false, log a warning and use the default builder.
- `verl/utils/tokenizer/continuous_token.py`: `require_token_id` also treats a tokenizer's `unk_token_id` as missing (HF tokenizers with an unk token return it for unknown strings instead of `None`), including when the id comes back wrapped in a one-element list. The unk token itself is still accepted.
- `tests/utils/test_continuous_token_on_cpu.py`: new cases listed above.

- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not needed: bug fix, no user-facing config or API change.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: new `*_on_cpu.py` tests run in `cpu_unit_tests.yml`; the end-to-end GRPO run above needs a GPU and the R1-Distill model, so it is not added to CI.
- [x] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)

I think the fallback target is not safe yet. Missing `<|im_end|>` proves that the tokenizer does not implement Qwen ChatML, but it does not prove that `ContinuousTokenBuilder` implements the checkpoint's conversation protocol.

In particular, #7637 already documents a concrete regression for `DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B`: its tool template concatenates `function['arguments']` as a string. The default builder creates synthetic tool-call arguments as `{}`, while `DeepSeekContinuousTokenBuilder` uses `"{}"` (from #7630). With this PR, that checkpoint will construct successfully and then fail on the first tool append with a `TypeError`. The GSM8K E2E run does not exercise tools, and the PR explicitly says that default-builder token boundaries were not evaluated.

There is a second issue in `_tokenizer_defines_token`: catching every `ValueError` from `require_token_id` also treats malformed results (multiple IDs, negative IDs, wrong types) as “token absent” and silently falls back. Only an explicit missing/unk-token condition should be recoverable; tokenizer contract errors should still surface.

I suggest keeping the `unk_token_id` validation, but not merging the generic default fallback. Safer options are:

1. expose/use an explicit `continuous_token.model_family` override and fail with actionable guidance (the direction previously preferred on #7638/#7639); or
2. if automatic routing is desired, use an exact DeepSeek tokenizer-protocol signature (`<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` and `<｜Assistant｜>` present, `<|im_end|>` absent) and select `DeepSeekContinuousTokenBuilder`, not the default builder.

Whichever route is chosen should add template-equivalence tests comparing incremental rendering with full `apply_chat_template`, including first and later tool turns for R1-0528-Qwen3 and the older R1-Distill-Qwen checkpoints. The later-turn `is_output_first` gap tracked in #7636 also still needs consideration.

I think the fallback target is not safe yet. Missing `<|im_end|>` proves that the tokenizer does not implement Qwen ChatML, but it does not prove that `ContinuousTokenBuilder` implements the checkpoint's conversation protocol.

In particular, #7637 already documents a concrete regression for `DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B`: its tool template concatenates `function['arguments']` as a string. The default builder creates synthetic tool-call arguments as `{}`, while `DeepSeekContinuousTokenBuilder` uses `"{}"` (from #7630). With this PR, that checkpoint will construct successfully and then fail on the first tool append with a `TypeError`. The GSM8K E2E run does not exercise tools, and the PR explicitly says that default-builder token boundaries were not evaluated.

There is a second issue in `_tokenizer_defines_token`: catching every `ValueError` from `require_token_id` also treats malformed results (multiple IDs, negative IDs, wrong types) as “token absent” and silently falls back. Only an explicit missing/unk-token condition should be recoverable; tokenizer contract errors should still surface.

I suggest keeping the `unk_token_id` validation, but not merging the generic default fallback. Safer options are:

1. expose/use an explicit `continuous_token.model_family` override and fail with actionable guidance (the direction previously preferred on #7638/#7639); or
2. if automatic routing is desired, use an exact DeepSeek tokenizer-protocol signature (`<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` and `<｜Assistant｜>` present, `<|im_end|>` absent) and select `DeepSeekContinuousTokenBuilder`, not the default builder.

Whichever route is chosen should add template-equivalence tests comparing incremental rendering with full `apply_chat_template`, including first and later tool turns for R1-0528-Qwen3 and the older R1-Distill-Qwen checkpoints. The later-turn `is_output_first` gap tracked in #7636 also still needs consideration.
